'''York:''' {{legend0|#7996e2|50–60%}} {{legend0|#6674de|60–70%}} | title = Governor | before_election = [[Lincoln Almond]] | before_party = Republican Party (United States) | after_election = [[Donald Carcieri]] | after_party = Republican Party (United States) }} {{ElectionsRI}} The '''2002 Rhode Island gubernatorial election''' took place on November 5, 2002. Incumbent [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] governor [[Lincoln Almond]] was term-limited. Republican [[Donald Carcieri]] won the open seat, defeating [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democrat]] [[Myrth York]]. In the Republican primary election, Carcieri defeated James Bennett, who had won the endorsement of the state Republican Party.{{cite news |url=http://www.ripr.org/post/fung-moves-closer-capturing-republican-governor-endorsement#stream/0 |title=Fung moves closer to capturing Republican governor endorsement |publisher=Rhode Island Public Radio |date=2014-06-20 |archive-date=August 3, 2016 |access-date=July 23, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160803203721/http://ripr.org/post/fung-moves-closer-capturing-republican-governor-endorsement#stream/0 |url-status=dead }} The 2002 campaign was particularly costly to York as she spent $3.8 million of her own money to finance what was to be her last bid for elected office. A key turning point in the campaign was when York criticized Carcieri for the actions of businesses he had been associated with but refused to answer Carcieri's request that she reveal what companies her personal assets were invested in.{{Cite web |last=Fenton |first=Josh |title=Myrth York Leads New Anti-Cianci Group and Launches TV Ad |url=https://www.golocalprov.com/politics/myrth-york-leads-new-anti-cianci-group-and-launches-tv-ad |access-date=2022-12-16 |website=GoLocalProv |language=en}} ==Republican primary== A Republican primary was held on September 10. ===Candidates=== *[[Donald Carcieri]], businessman *Jim Bennett ===Results=== {{Election box begin no change | title = Republican primary results{{Cite web |url=http://www.elections.state.ri.us/elections/results/2002/statewideprimary/summary.php |title=Rhode Island Board of Elections: Elections & Voting |access-date=2011-04-23 |archive-date=2011-09-28 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110928133420/http://www.elections.state.ri.us/elections/results/2002/statewideprimary/summary.php |url-status=dead }} }} {{Election box winning candidate with party link no change | candidate = Donald Carcieri | party = Republican Party (United States) | votes = 17,227 | percentage = 66.91 }} {{Election box candidate with party link no change | candidate = James S.
